sub_scenario.family: travel recovery physiology versus high-stakes scheduling
sub_scenario.one_line: international arbitration counsel: poor fit as calendared

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the cross-examination outline and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The hearing bundle review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Long-haul travel before document-review days costs nothing measurable.
Document work survives arrival days.
Survives them completely.
Someone new shadowed me in the chambers this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the witness schedules into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
My own hearing notes flag it: the one cross I conducted the day after a long-haul arrival, I missed a documented contradiction I had personally outlined the week before.
You missed your own prepared point.
My own point, in my own outline, highlighted.
Cross-examinations on full rest are the strongest part of my practice.
The skill is not in question.
Only its fuel supply.
I archived last cycle's notes on the hearing bundle and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
Co-counsel caught the miss on day three and salvaged it, but the tribunal's interim summary had already framed the issue against us.
The cost was real and recorded.
Recorded in an interim summary, no less.
A vendor call about the cross-examination outline ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the chambers checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the witness schedules.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the hearing bundle records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The Singapore calendar sets my cross for the morning after my earliest possible arrival; the prior hearing in Geneva makes any earlier flight impossible.
The calendar locks you into the arrival-morning slot.
Locks it, both ends.
I sketched next week's plan for the witness schedules before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the cross-examination outline updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
This cross concerns the quantum expert, the highest-stakes witness of the entire arbitration.
Maximum stakes in the compromised window.
Maximum, precisely there.
I compared two options for the hearing bundle tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the chambers handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Co-counsel asked directly whether I should keep the first-morning cross slot as the calendar stands. Is that slot right for me?
